name: Longevity
boundaries: Longevity: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: Safe systemic reversal of all hallmarks
original_dispositions.reason: Covered by LON-02, with molecular repair in LON-05. The revised criterion is restored function and safety; simultaneous normalization of every proposed hallmark is not assumed necessary.
Covered, in broader and testable form, by LON-01. A single root cause is a possibility, not an established requirement.

original_dispositions.original_title: Mechanism and clearance of all senescent cells
original_dispositions.reason: Covered as a possible route to LON-02 or LON-03, not added separately. Removing a cell population alone does not establish systemic rejuvenation, and eliminating all senescent cells is not shown to be necessary or safe.
Added as LON-07, broadened to include removal of harmful signals and other causal circulating processes. Successful organism-wide rejuvenation would overlap LON-02.
Covered as a possible route to LON-02. A clock reset or altered gene expression alone is insufficient to establish restored organismal function.
Added as LON-06, without assuming that one mechanism explains all long-lived species or that transfer to humans follows automatically.

Covered as a possible component of LON-02. Not added separately: a universal regulator is speculative, and restored stem-cell measures alone would not establish whole-organism rejuvenation or regeneration of every tissue.

Covered as a possible mechanism or component of LON-02 and LON-03, with direct repair of particular damaged proteins potentially overlapping LON-05. Not added separately: restoring protein quality control would not by itself establish cures for the listed diseases.

Covered by LON-04, specifically the stronger requirement that treatment-induced changes predict later clinical outcomes. Accurate individual prediction of remaining healthspan is related but is not established by that surrogate alone.

original_dispositions.original_title: A drug extending healthy mammalian lifespan by at least 50%
original_dispositions.reason: The consequential human capability is covered by LON-03. Not added separately: 50% is an unsupported threshold, and even a large effect in another mammal would not itself prove decades of human benefit or secure regulatory approval.

reconciliation_change_log.change: LON-01–LON-05 retained: Their identities and proposed demonstrations remain intact.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The notes clarified that a single root cause is not assumed, separated clinical outcomes from molecular measures, and made the human and in-vivo evidence gaps explicit.
The full 2026 paper was accessible through PubMed Central during this review, improving on the first pass’s abstract-only access. Its findings remain ex vivo.

Cross-species identification and transfer of exceptional longevity mechanisms is a distinct causal and engineering achievement, supported by a mouse transfer experiment but far from transfer of negligible senescence.
Causal control of circulating aging signals is a distinct systemic mechanism and research capability, even though a successful therapy could overlap LON-02 or LON-03.

GeroScience volume 47, issue 1 is dated February 2025, and its listed special issues differ from the historical description. The claimed ten-item ranking is unsupported by the inspected issue page. The other historical links could not be substantively inspected with the available web tool and are not used as evidence for that ranking.
